title: Clean Sleep Session Text Fields
prompt: You are working with a sleep tracking app modeled on public health survey datasets (NHANES, BRFSS). The `sleep_sessions` table stores each night's sleep data. The `session_notes` column contains free-text notes entered by users that often have inconsistent formatting: extra whitespace, inconsistent capitalization, and embedded email addresses. The `user_email` column sometimes has leading or trailing spaces. Write a query that extracts and cleans these fields for reporting. For each session, extract the username (the part before the '@' in the email address), clean the email address by removing any leading or trailing spaces, capitalize the first letter of each word in the session notes while removing extra internal spaces, and extract the domain name (the part after the '@') from the email. Return columns `session_id`, `username`, `clean_email`, `clean_notes`, and `domain`. Order the results by `session_id` ascending. Some session notes may be NULL; if so, return NULL for `clean_notes`.

display.context: You are working with a sleep tracking app modeled on public health survey datasets (NHANES, BRFSS).
display.task: Write a query that extracts and cleans user email addresses and session notes for reporting.

table_notes.sleep_sessions: holds one row per sleep session with user email and free-text notes

output_field_notes.session_id: unique identifier for the sleep session
output_field_notes.username: the portion of the email address before the at-sign
output_field_notes.clean_email: the email address with leading and trailing spaces removed
output_field_notes.clean_notes: the session notes with each word capitalized and extra spaces removed, or NULL if the original note was NULL
output_field_notes.domain: the portion of the email address after the at-sign

field_logic: username: extract everything before the at-sign in the email address
clean_email: remove any leading or trailing spaces from the email
clean_notes: capitalize the first letter of each word and collapse multiple spaces into one, or return NULL if the note is NULL
domain: extract everything after the at-sign in the email address
edge_cases: If session_notes is NULL, then clean_notes should also be NULL.
If the email has leading or trailing spaces, those must be removed.
If session_notes has multiple consecutive spaces, those must be collapsed to single spaces.
display.filter_note: All rows from sleep_sessions are included.
display.order_by_note: Results are ordered by session_id in ascending order.

schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE sleep_sessions (session_id INT PRIMARY KEY, user_email VARCHAR(100), sleep_score INT, session_notes TEXT);

composite_moves: parse email to extract username and domain
normalize and capitalize session notes text

hints: You will need to use string functions to extract parts of the email address around the '@' symbol.
The TRIM function removes leading and trailing spaces. INITCAP capitalizes the first letter of each word. Use REGEXP_REPLACE to collapse multiple spaces into one.

Use SPLIT_PART(user_email, '@', 1) to get the username and SPLIT_PART(user_email, '@', 2) to get the domain. For the notes, first trim and collapse spaces with REGEXP_REPLACE(session_notes, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), then apply INITCAP. Wrap the notes transformation in a way that preserves NULLs.
answer_key: SELECT session_id, SPLIT_PART(TRIM(user_email), '@', 1) AS username, TRIM(user_email) AS clean_email, CASE WHEN session_notes IS NOT NULL THEN INITCAP(TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(session_notes, '\s+', ' ', 'g'))) ELSE NULL END AS clean_notes, SPLIT_PART(TRIM(user_email), '@', 2) AS domain FROM sleep_sessions ORDER BY session_id;

_meta.scenario: a sleep tracking app tracking sleep score and goal achievement
